gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the parking-mode hardwire kit for each camera costs or which models the maker says it fits: VIOFO's HK4 is $17.99, fits the A229 Pro, excludes the mini-USB A119 V3/A129 models and (per VIOFO's HK6 listing) does not do hybrid parking; DDPAI's $29.99 fuse-tap kit covers every DDPAI camera except the Z100 Master; ROVE's Dual Pro rear camera and rear cables fit that model only.
standout_why: Compared against productbible.com (front-and-rear), roadgearlab.com, the-gadgeteer.com, digitalcameraworld.com and knowledgelib.io. Product Bible and knowledgelib name the HK4 for VIOFO but give no kit price and no exclusion list. RoadGearLab names only the HK6 (for the A119M Pro) and says of the 70mai only that parking needs 'its hardwire kit'. The Gadgeteer names no kit. None gives a rear-cable length or the longer-cable options (Product Bible says only 'check the length included'). None covers any DDPAI or Vantrue S1 Pro Max kit pairing. ChatGPT's own answer says 'budget another $20-$40' without naming a kit or price. caranddriver.com could not be fetched, so it is not in the comparison.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick; the kit price is what holds or breaks the $250 line once parking mode is wanted. VIOFO's kit adds $17.99 to the A229 Pro 2CH, DDPAI's adds $29.99 (or $10-$20 as a store '+ Hardwire Kit' variant on its other models), and Vantrue's cheapest adds $24.99, which would take the S1 Pro Max 4K+4K ($239.99 on 2026-11-21, your table) to $264.98, over budget. Two price flags came out of the same store reads, both unverified at variant level because the product pages returned HTTP 429: store.ddpai.com listed the N5 Pro at $259.00 (list $379.00), not the $179.00 in your record of 2026-11-17, and viofo.com listed the A229 Pro 2CH at $349.99, over budget at the maker's store. The N5 Pro price needs a re-read before the page goes out.
